claims.claim: ITW's 2026 operating signal strengthened between Q1 and Q2: organic growth accelerated from 0.4% to 4.5%, with Q2 capex-related segments led by double-digit organic growth in Welding and Test & Measurement and Electronics.
ITW raised full-year 2026 revenue, organic-growth and EPS guidance after Q2, providing a primary-source signal that execution was running ahead of its February baseline expectations.

factors.name: capex-cycle exposure
factors.basis: Q2 disclosed accelerating demand in Welding and Test & Measurement and Electronics.

factors.name: operating model leverage
factors.basis: Q2 operating margin reached 26.7% while enterprise initiatives contributed 120 bps.

risks.risk: Demand acceleration is uneven across end markets and remains exposed to industrial/capex cyclicality.
Pricing offset raw-material inflation in Q2, but timing lags modestly diluted margins and could recur.

unknowns.unknown: Durability of Q2 capex acceleration into 2027 is not established by current evidence.

claims.claim: ITW raised 2026 EPS guidance at both Q1 and Q2; after Q2 the range was $11.35-$11.55, with revenue growth guided to 4-5% and organic growth to 3-4%.
Q2 operating income of $1.15B was the most profitable quarter in company history and free cash flow increased 41% year over year to $631M.

factors.name: guidance conversion
factors.basis: Two successive guidance increases and accelerating Q2 organic growth support execution credibility.

factors.name: cash conversion checkpoint
factors.basis: Q2 FCF improved strongly, but management still expects full-year FCF above 100% of net income, leaving a second-half conversion test.

risks.risk: Raised expectations increase disappointment sensitivity if organic growth or margin expansion fades.

unknowns.unknown: No Scout valuation/entry conclusion is asserted; canonical valuation remains Alpha-owned.
